extracted.intended_audience: Federal agencies and officials preparing documents for publication in the Federal Register and the Code of Federal Regulations; legal practitioners and public users of the CFR/Federal Register
extracted.subtask_description: Rules, policies, and procedural criteria for filing, publishing, indexing, and reproducing documents in the Federal Register and for preparing material for codification in the Code of Federal Regulations (CFR). Covers what must be filed/published, formats, timing, incorporation by reference, indexing, and related public-access rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions (Document; Document having general applicability and legal effect; Filing)
rubrics_metrics.description: As used in this chapter: 'Document' includes presidential proclamations or executive orders, and any rule, regulation, order, certificate, code of fair competition, license, notice, or similar instrument issued by an agency. 'Document having general applicability and legal effect' means any document issued under proper authority prescribing a penalty or conduct, conferring rights, privileges, authority, or imposing an obligation, and relevant to the general public or a class. 'Filing' means making a document available for public inspection at the Office of the Federal Register; a document is filed only after it has been received, processed and assigned a publication date according to the schedule in part 17.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These definitional terms determine which materials are subject to the chapter's filing and publication rules and when a document is considered 'filed' for public inspection and publication purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director's authority to return documents
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may return to the issuing agency any document submitted for publication if, in the Director’s judgment, the document does not meet the minimum requirements of this chapter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should ensure submissions satisfy the chapter's minimum requirements (form, authority, timeliness, etc.) to avoid return. The Director is delegated authority to administer the chapter generally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documents required to be filed and published
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents required to be filed for public inspection and published include: (a) Presidential proclamations and Executive orders in the numbered series and each other Presidential document the President submits or orders published; (b) each document or class of documents required to be published by act of Congress; (c) each document having general applicability and legal effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a document falls into any of these categories it must be filed with the Office of the Federal Register and published in the FEDERAL REGISTER.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication policy: timeliness vs accuracy/usability/costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Each document required or authorized to be filed for publication shall be published in the FEDERAL REGISTER as promptly as possible, within limitations imposed by considerations of accuracy, usability, and reasonable costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should balance speed with accuracy, ensuring documents are usable and published within reasonable cost constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication not authorized (prohibitions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Chapter 15 does not apply to treaties, conventions, protocols, or other international agreements or their proclamations by the President. Chapter 15 prohibits publication in the FEDERAL REGISTER of comments or news items. The Director may not accept any document for filing unless it is the official action of the agency concerned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must not submit non-authoritative papers, comments, or news items for publication; international agreements are not published under chapter 15.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director may publish other documents in public interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever the Director considers that publication of a document not covered by the required list would be in the public interest, the Director may allow it to be filed for public inspection and published in the FEDERAL REGISTER.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is discretionary authority; agencies may request publication of atypical documents, but acceptance is by Director determination of public interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public inspection: availability and procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents filed pursuant to law are available for public inspection at 800 North Capitol Street, NW., suite 700, Washington, DC, during Office hours. There are no formal inspection procedures or requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The public may inspect filed documents during Office hours; agencies should ensure timely filing to allow inspection prior to publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing timeline and notation requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director shall cause each document received to be filed for public inspection not later than the working day preceding the publication day for that document. The Director shall place on original and certified copies of each document a notation of the day and hour when it was filed and made available for public inspection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should submit with sufficient lead time to permit filing at least one working day before publication; filing dates/times are recorded on originals and certified copies.

rubrics_metrics.name: What constitutes 'filed' for public inspection
rubrics_metrics.description: A document is filed only after it has been received, processed and assigned a publication date according to the schedule in part 17 of this chapter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Merely submitting a document does not constitute filing; agencies need confirmation that processing and a publication date have been assigned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public may obtain photocopies; reproduction/certification governed by NARA regs
rubrics_metrics.description: Photocopies of documents or excerpts may be made at the inspection desk. The regulations for public use of records in the National Archives (36 CFR parts 1252–1258) govern furnishing reproductions and certificates of authentication; advance payment of fees may be required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users should follow NARA fee/payment procedures when requesting certified reproductions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categories of documents (placement in Federal Register)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each document published in the FEDERAL REGISTER shall be placed under one category: (a) The President; (b) Rules and regulations (documents having general applicability and legal effect except Presidential); (c) Proposed rules (notices of proposed rulemaking under section 553 or other law); (d) Notices (miscellaneous documents not covered by other categories).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must indicate appropriate category for each submission so the Office can place it under the correct heading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplement to the CFR and codification linkage
rubrics_metrics.description: The FEDERAL REGISTER serves as a daily supplement to the Code of Federal Regulations. Each document subject to codification and published in a daily issue shall be keyed to the Code of Federal Regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory documents intended for codification should include clear indicia (e.g., parts/sections) so they can be properly keyed to the CFR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Periodic updating of the Code: frequency and cutoff
rubrics_metrics.description: Each book of the Code shall be updated at least once each calendar year. If no change occurred, a notation may serve as the supplement for that year. More frequent updating may occur when content is substantially superseded. Each updated title will reflect amendments published in the FEDERAL REGISTER on or before the 'As of' date (cutoff).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should plan rulemaking and codification with the CFR 'as of' cutoff dates in mind to ensure amendments appear in the intended annual update.

rubrics_metrics.name: Orderly development of the Code (title establishment/rearrangement)
rubrics_metrics.description: To assure orderly development, the Director may establish new titles in the Code and rearrange existing titles and subordinate assignments, but must consult with each agency directly affected before taking action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies affected by proposed structural changes will be consulted prior to Director action; agencies may engage in consultations to influence organization of the Code.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indexes and ancillaries: index and lists requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Each daily issue shall be appropriately indexed; analytical subject indexes shall be published as current as practicable and cumulated at least once each calendar year; each daily issue shall carry a numerical list of parts of the CFR specifically affected by documents in that issue and (starting with second issue of month) a cumulated list for that month; a monthly list of sections affected is published cumulatively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should provide clear citations to parts/sections affected so indexes and lists accurately reflect changes; the Office may prepare additional indexes, digests, and guides as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forms of publication (formats)
rubrics_metrics.description: The FEDERAL REGISTER is published in paper, microfiche, and online on GPO Access (44 U.S.C. 4101). The e-CFR is an unofficial, regularly updated editorial compilation available online.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should consider multiple distribution formats; subscribers and users should note that e-CFR is unofficial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Daily publication and delivery schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: There shall be an edition of the FEDERAL REGISTER published for each official Federal working day. The Government Printing Office shall distribute the FEDERAL REGISTER by delivery or deposit at a post office at or before 9 a.m. on the publication day (with Monday issues deposited by preceding Saturday).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication and distribution follow strict timing rules; agencies should schedule submissions to align with daily production timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation by reference: legal effect and approval criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorporation by reference allows agencies to meet publication requirements by referring to materials published elsewhere; legally treated as if published in full (5 U.S.C. 552(a)). The Director will approve an incorporation by reference only when the requirements of 1 CFR part 51 are met. Approval is based on elements including: (a) the incorporation will substantially reduce the volume of material published in the Federal Register; (b) the matter incorporated is in fact available to the extent necessary to afford fairness and uniformity in the administrative process; (c) the incorporating document is drafted and submitted for publication in accordance with 1 CFR part 51.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies seeking approval must ensure availability and proper drafting/submission per part 51, and document how incorporation reduces publication volume; incorporated material carries the force of law when approved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unavailable incorporated material: remedy
rubrics_metrics.description: If material listed as an approved incorporation by reference cannot be located, contact the issuing agency; if still not available, notify the Director of the Federal Register at the provided address or phone number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should ensure public availability of incorporated materials; the Office provides a contact path if availability problems arise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unrestricted use and republication of CFR material
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person may reproduce or republish, without restriction, any material appearing in any regular or special edition of the FEDERAL REGISTER. There are no restrictions on the republication of material appearing in the Code of Federal Regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reproducers should note other rules (e.g., NARA seal/logo restrictions and ISBN prefix rules) that govern official labeling and use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of NARA seals and CFR logo and ISBN prefix restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: It is prohibited to use NARA's official seal and the stylized Code of Federal Regulations logo on any republication of this material without express written permission of the Archivist. Use of the 0–16 ISBN prefix is for U.S. Government Publishing Office Official Editions only; reprinted editions should be clearly labeled as a copy with a new ISBN.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publishers and reprinters must obtain permission for use of official seals/logos and must not use the GPO ISBN prefix except for official editions; violations may be subject to criminal penalties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information services limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Office staff provide information concerning publications and original acts/documents filed, except they may not summarize or interpret substantive text of any act or document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users seeking legal interpretation should contact the issuing agency; Office staff can provide reference assistance only, not substantive interpretations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective and expiration dates: care in determining actual effective date
rubrics_metrics.description: Publication dates and effective dates are usually not the same; care must be exercised in determining the actual effective date. Where effective date is beyond the CFR cutoff date a note will reflect the future effective date. When a Federal Register regulation states a date certain for expiration, an appropriate note will be inserted following the text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users and agencies must check effective-date statements and any notes in the CFR to determine legal applicability on given dates.
